evals.prompt: I just finished building the inbox feature on this branch. Can you walk me through my changes against main? /diff-review main
evals.expected_output: Full 4-checkpoint interactive walkthrough with large-diff scope limiting, tree-based browser overview, optional dedicated flow page, focused file walks, concerns, and notes file.
expectations: Recognizes 45 files / ~2600 lines as a large diff and triggers the scope limit (asks for walk order or confirmation before proceeding)
Produces a tree-based Diff Overview HTML with rolled-up folder summaries instead of the old file table
When a cross-layer flow exists, emits a separate dedicated flow page rather than embedding the Mermaid graph into the overview page
Asks the developer about intent before proceeding to the walkthrough
References or creates a notes file path under .claude/docs/diff-notes/
All 4 checkpoints appear in sequence (Checkpoint 1 through Checkpoint 4)
Shows actual git diff hunks in Checkpoint 2 (not just prose descriptions of what changed)
Surfaces at least one concern in Checkpoint 3 using the ⚠️ Concern format with file:line reference
Includes a Progress Tracker table with file status indicators

evals.prompt:
/diff-review

I just edited the inbox page component and the mock service — walk me through what I changed
evals.expected_output: Conversation-mode walkthrough of 2 files with behavioral summaries, prediction questions, correction handling, data flow analysis, and concerns.
expectations: Correctly identifies conversation mode and scopes to the 2 specified files (inbox.component.ts and inbox-mock.service.ts)
Each file walkthrough includes a behavioral summary with 'What changed', 'Where in flow', or 'Data in → out' fields
Asks at least one non-trivial prediction question in Checkpoint 2 (not 'what does this do?' but something specific)
When the developer's prediction is partially wrong, names the gap and explains the correct behavior before advancing
Checkpoint 3 traces at least one data path and names invariants (what must be true)
Concerns include file:line references so the developer knows exactly where to look

evals.expected_output: Graceful handling of no-changes edge case: clear communication, alternative offered, no broken output.
expectations: Clearly states that no conversation edits were found AND no unstaged/staged changes exist
Offers a graceful alternative or asks the developer what they want to review (does not just stop)
Does not produce broken output, empty checkpoints, or error messages — handles the edge case cleanly
